title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
title_zh: 从FAIR到AI-FAIR：面向AI赋能科学的元数据优先基础设施

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question–Data–Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow 1 1 1 Code available at: github.com/FAIR4AI-Bio/evaluator . that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能（AI）技术及其能力在过去几年中迅速发展，引发了生物科学与生态科学领域的广泛关注与应用。 然而，为生态学和生物多样性科学中AI工作流提供基础的数据基础设施与计算资源仍然碎片化。 此外，价值的流动在很大程度上仍是单向的：数据从采集者出发，经由数据仓库和聚合平台进入模型，最终形成研究成果或管理行动。 衍生价值，例如经过修订的分类体系、标注、质量标记和洞见，很少回流到数据来源社群。 我们提出对原始FAIR原则的一个扩展，以满足AI就绪基础设施的需求：AI-FAIR元数据标准，该标准将AI赋能的科学置于双向的「问题–数据–模型」三角情境之中。 这一框架旨在促进跨多样化藏品集合的大规模基于内容的分析，并确保生成数据的科学家能够从基于其数据的AI赋能进展中受益。 与这些标准相配套，我们引入一个智能体评估工作流¹（代码可在 github.com/FAIR4AI-Bio/evaluator 获取。），它既依据AI-FAIR和传统FAIR标准对现有数据集进行评级，也在关键元数据缺失或不完整时提供可操作的反馈。 这一模块化数据集评估工具与适合具体领域的检查清单相结合，将这些原则转化为对机器学习就绪度、面向特定任务的AI就绪度、可追溯性以及符合伦理和CARE原则的数据管护的可复用评估。 通过这一方法，我们旨在建立一个由社区共同塑造的体系，以闭合「模型–数据」循环，使AI也能反哺数据，从而进一步推动科学发现。

paragraphs.en: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing how research in the domains of ecology and biodiversity science is conducted ( Pollock et al., 2025 ). However, current workflows still rely on data infrastructure built primarily to encourage researcher data contributions rather than to prioritize the machine-readability and cross-dataset interoperability that facilitate data reuse ( Crystal-Ornelas et al., 2022 ). In both domains, data span species occurrences, images, audio, genomic sequences, sensor observations, field measurements, synthesized species biological information, and environmental covariates ( Feng et al., 2025 ). Heterogeneous communities produce these assets using different terminologies, collecting data at varied spatial and temporal scales, releasing data under diverse licenses and governance frameworks, and storing data in siloed repositories. Fragmented storage, inconsistent formats, limited interoperability, and incomplete scientific context have long presented hurdles for ecological synthesis efforts ( O’Brien et al., 2021 ), and these barriers have become no more tractable as ecologists develop AI-enabled workflows ( Mishra, 2026 ). We refer to these persistent obstacles to scientific discovery as the FAIR-gap .
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能（AI）正在迅速改变生态学与生物多样性科学领域的研究方式（Pollock et al., 2025）。 然而，当前的工作流程仍依赖主要为了鼓励研究人员贡献数据而构建的数据基础设施，而非优先考虑有助于数据复用的机器可读性与跨数据集互操作性（Crystal-Ornelas et al., 2022）。 在这两个领域中，数据涵盖物种出现记录、图像、音频、基因组序列、传感器观测、野外测量、综合的物种生物学信息以及环境协变量（Feng et al., 2025）。 不同的社区使用不同的术语来产出这些数据资产，在不同时空尺度上收集数据，以多样的许可协议和治理框架发布数据，并将数据存储在相互隔离的存储库中。 分散的存储、不一致的格式、有限的互操作性以及不完整的科学背景长期以来一直是生态学综合研究的障碍（O'Brien et al., 2021），而当生态学家开发由人工智能赋能的工作流程时，这些障碍并没有变得更容易解决（Mishra, 2026）。 我们将这些持续阻碍科学发现的障碍称为 FAIR 差距（FAIR-gap）。

paragraphs.en: While the original FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles ( Wilkinson et al., 2016 ) remain necessary, they are not sufficient criteria to guide AI-ready infrastructure in the sciences and overcome the FAIR-gap ( Huerta et al., 2023 ; Clark et al., 2026 ; Shehu & Nussinov, 2026 ). AI-enabled, data-driven science requires machine-actionable access and interpretation at the appropriate scale. Even a findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable dataset may require extensive human intervention to determine whether the data are appropriate and permitted for a scientific task, or to connect augmented information (e.g., errors flagged or enhancements) back to the original source.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管最初的 FAIR（可发现、可访问、可互操作、可重用）原则（Wilkinson et al., 2016）仍然必要，但它们并不足以作为指导科学领域 AI 就绪基础设施并克服 FAIR 差距的标准（Huerta et al., 2023；Clark et al., 2026；Shehu & Nussinov, 2026）。 AI 赋能的数据驱动科学需要在适当规模上的机器可操作访问与解读。 即使是一个可发现、可访问、可互操作且可重用的数据集，也可能需要大量的人工干预，才能确定这些数据是否适合并被允许用于某项科学任务，或将增补的信息（例如标记的错误或增强内容）关联回原始来源。

paragraphs.en: Extensive global museum digitization efforts, growing community science platform engagement, and increasing accessibility and sensitivity of sensor technologies have produced vast quantities of data faster than can be processed and analyzed through traditional methods. As AI-driven search is increasingly replacing traditional algorithms, FAIR-gapped data risk exclusion from search results, preventing researchers from even considering them. Collecting and curating biodiversity data is labor-intensive; they should not be excluded from consideration because researchers (or AI agents) cannot find or access them, nor should they be misattributed or used for analyses they do not support. The time required to manually sift through these data is rapidly exceeding the capacity of individual researchers. Moreover, the effort, resources, and time that goes into data collection are translated into scientific value and meaning only when those data are used, and attribution is a recognition of those efforts.
paragraphs.zh: 全球范围内大规模的博物馆数字化工作、社区科学平台参与度的不断提升，以及传感器技术可及性和灵敏度的日益提高，所产生的海量数据的增长速度，已超出了传统方法能够处理和分析的能力。 随着 AI 驱动的搜索日益取代传统算法，存在 FAIR 缺口的数据面临被排除在搜索结果之外的风险，使研究人员甚至无法考虑这些数据。 收集和整理生物多样性数据需要大量人力；这些数据不应因为研究人员（或智能体）无法找到或访问它们而被排除在考虑范围之外，也不应被错误归属或用于其并不支持的分析。 人工筛选这些数据所需的时间正在迅速超出单个研究人员的承受能力。 此外，只有当这些数据被使用时，投入数据收集的努力、资源和时间才能转化为科学价值和意义，而署名归属正是对这些努力的认可。

paragraphs.en: Enabling automated assessment of data for scientific use (e.g., using an agentic AI system to perform a broad scale analysis across multiple databases and flag those of interest for manual review) provides a force-multiplier, but this capability requires increased and more consistent documentation of the datasets. Drawing from the FAIR4AI framework ( Huerta et al., 2023 ) and the FAIR data principles ( Wilkinson et al., 2016 ), we define AI-FAIR metadata criteria as the key to AI-enabled science with bidirectional value. Rather than developing a new prescriptive data specification, we complement ongoing work by Bridge2AI ( Clark et al., 2026 ) and the FAIR 2 Alliance ( n.d. ). Our framework focuses on foundational metadata components that data providers can integrate into their chosen standards to accelerate scientific discovery and ensure lasting value.
paragraphs.zh: 启用面向科学用途的数据自动化评估（例如，使用智能体 AI 系统跨多个数据库进行大规模分析，并标记出需要人工审查的相关数据）提供了一种力量倍增器，但这一能力需要对数据集进行更多且更一致的文档化。 借鉴 FAIR4AI 框架（Huerta et al., 2023）和 FAIR 数据原则（Wilkinson et al., 2016），我们将 AI-FAIR 元数据标准定义为具有双向价值的 AI 赋能科学的关键。 我们没有开发新的规定性数据规范，而是对 Bridge2AI（Clark et al., 2026）和 FAIR 2 联盟（n.d.）正在进行的工作加以补充。 我们的框架聚焦于基础的元数据组件，数据提供方可以将其整合到各自选定的标准中，以加速科学发现并确保持久的价值。

paragraphs.en: The FAIR4AI-Bio network was conceived to address the FAIR-gap by placing the data providers and users at the center of the solutions. This process includes hosting a series of workshops to understand requirements for AI-ready data infrastructure in ecology, biodiversity science, and related fields. The guiding mission through these workshops is to create a community-informed system for unifying biodiversity data at scale, one that promotes trust and encourages the exchange of data. We started by creating an inventory of the platforms and tools used by data producers, providers, managers, and scientists who work with ecological and biodiversity data. We then gathered feedback from the workshop community to identify the challenges and critical blockers encountered with these platforms and tools, and synthesized these into a collection of requirements to address the FAIR-gap: our AI-FAIR framework. This community relies heavily on multimodal data integration for analyses, and addressing this complexity of use-cases will support the design of a robust prototype of the AI-FAIR framework.
paragraphs.zh: FAIR4AI-Bio 网络的构想是为了解决 FAIR 差距，其方法是将数据提供者和使用者置于解决方案的中心。 这一过程包括举办一系列研讨会，以了解生态学、生物多样性科学及相关领域对 AI 就绪数据基础设施的需求。 贯穿这些研讨会的指导性使命，是创建一个由社区共同构建的系统，用于大规模统一生物多样性数据，促进信任并鼓励数据交换。 我们首先创建了一份平台与工具清单，涵盖处理生态和生物多样性数据的数据生产者、提供者、管理者及科学家所使用的平台与工具。 随后，我们收集了研讨会社区的反馈，以识别在使用这些平台和工具时遇到的挑战与关键阻碍，并将其归纳为一组需求集合，以解决 FAIR 差距：即我们的 AI-FAIR 框架。 该社区的分析工作高度依赖多模态数据整合，应对这一复杂的使用场景将有助于设计出一个健壮的 AI-FAIR 框架原型。

sents.en: We then gathered feedback from the workshop community to identify the challenges and critical blockers encountered with these platforms and tools, and synthesized these into a collection of requirements to address the FAIR-gap: our AI-FAIR framework.
sents.zh: 随后，我们收集了研讨会社区的反馈，以识别在使用这些平台和工具时遇到的挑战与关键阻碍，并将其归纳为一组需求集合，以解决 FAIR 差距：即我们的 AI-FAIR 框架。

sents.en: This community relies heavily on multimodal data integration for analyses, and addressing this complexity of use-cases will support the design of a robust prototype of the AI-FAIR framework.
sents.zh: 该社区的分析工作高度依赖多模态数据整合，应对这一复杂的使用场景将有助于设计出一个健壮的 AI-FAIR 框架原型。

paragraphs.en: Dataset properties that extend from traditional FAIR principles to AI-FAIR specifically enable machines to use data with minimal human intervention. These include essential metadata to provide the context and controls required for scientifically valid and responsible use at scale. It is impractical to expect data publishers to anticipate the requirements for all possible AI-enabled uses of their data, but AI-FAIR criteria offer guidance for data publishers to provide enhanced metadata that enable more efficient, automated, and accurate inclusion of their data in AI workflows at scale (Figure 1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 从传统FAIR原则扩展至AI-FAIR的数据集属性，特别地使机器能够在最少人工干预的情况下使用数据。 这些属性包括必要的元数据，用于提供在规模化下实现科学有效且负责任使用所需的背景信息和控制手段。 期望数据发布者预见到其数据所有可能的AI赋能用途的要求是不切实际的，但AI-FAIR标准为数据发布者提供了指导，使其能够提供增强的元数据，从而使其数据能够以更高效、自动化且准确的方式被纳入大规模的AI工作流中（图1）。

paragraphs.en: The AI-FAIR perspective frames AI-enabled science as a Question-Data-Model triangle (Figure 2 ). In a complete system, every edge is bidirectional. Questions specify required data properties and model capabilities.

paragraphs.en: However, the data vertex remains mostly unidirectional: data flow from collectors to aggregators, to models, and finally to research products or management actions. At each transition, the provenance chain is often weakened or severed, exacerbating challenges in returning information to data sources. This degradation of provenance increases the risk of data leakage , where evaluation data are included in model training. Furthermore, solving this requires additional complex processing—such as perceptual hashing ( Zhou et al., 2025 )—to disentangle aggregated data that are no longer traceable to their sources. Without context resolution, scientists are limited in the conclusions they can draw from model results, further increasing the likelihood that value created downstream will not return to the people and systems that produced the data used to train and evaluate it.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，数据顶点的流动仍然大多是单向的：数据从采集者流向聚合者，再流向模型，最终流向研究成果或管理行动。 在每一次转换中，溯源链条往往被削弱或切断，加剧了将信息回馈给数据来源的挑战。 这种溯源的退化增加了数据泄露的风险，即评测数据被纳入模型训练之中。 此外，解决这一问题需要额外的复杂处理——例如感知哈希（Zhou et al., 2025）——以理清那些已无法追溯到其来源的聚合数据。 缺乏情境解析时，科学家从模型结果中能得出的结论将受到限制，进一步增加了下游创造的价值无法回馈给生产和用于训练与评测模型的数据的人员和系统的可能性。

paragraphs.en: We posit that data value roundtripping ( Larsson et al., 2019 ; Groom et al., 2022 ) must be prioritized in efforts to design distributed AI-ready infrastructure. As AI systems process data—aided by expert validation—enhancing metadata, harmonizing taxonomies, detecting and flagging anomalies, and identifying gaps, they generate intermediate products for which there must be a mechanism to provide these artifacts back to the source repositories. For example, large-scale synthesis in ecology and biodiversity science often involves correcting or aligning taxonomies; identifying bounding boxes for images; detecting and flagging data anomalies; filling gaps in time-series data; assimilating data from other sources, and augmenting labels. Without a provenance chain and standardized metadata detailing the returns desirable by a data collector, all such data augmentation will remain siloed in data archives specific to synthesis projects. Other synthesis efforts will be required to repeat similar processing, with little to no benefit flowing to source repositories, communities, or data producers.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为，在设计分布式AI就绪基础设施的努力中，必须优先考虑数据价值回流（Larsson et al., 2019; Groom et al., 2022）。 当AI系统处理数据时——在专家验证的辅助下——增强元数据、统一分类体系、检测并标记异常、识别数据缺口，它们会生成中间产物，必须有一种机制将这些产物回馈给源存储库。 例如，生态学与生物多样性科学中的大规模综合研究通常涉及校正或对齐分类体系；为图像标识边界框；检测并标记数据异常；填补时间序列数据中的缺口； assimilate 来自其他来源的数据；以及增补标签。 如果没有溯源链以及详细说明数据收集者所期望回馈内容的标准化元数据，所有这些数据增强都将孤立地留存在特定于综合项目的数据档案中。 其他综合研究将不得不重复类似的处理流程，而几乎没有任何收益回流到源存储库、社区或数据生产者。

paragraphs.en: Data sources should be able to incorporate new knowledge with versioning, provenance, and attribution, where appropriate. This, in turn benefits the downstream users and reduces redundant processing. Such an interconnected system has the potential to produce better inputs (e.g., time-series gaps filled, taxonomy aligned, errors corrected) to later workflows, creating a living knowledge system that improves through use .
paragraphs.zh: 数据源应能在适当情况下，通过版本管理、来源追溯和归属标注来纳入新知识。 这反过来会让下游用户受益，并减少重复处理。 这样一个相互关联的系统有可能为后续工作流提供更好的输入（例如填补时间序列缺口、对齐分类体系、纠正错误），从而形成一个在使用中不断完善的活知识系统。

paragraphs.en: The AI-FAIR framework suggests infrastructure priorities, which can be assessed using the AI-FAIR Checklist. This checklist was initially seeded from the ESIP AI-Readiness Checklist ( ESIP Data Readiness Cluster, 2023 ) and the Imageomics Dataset Card Checklist ( Campolongo et al., 2026 ). Building on these foundations, we engaged workshop participants in the evaluation of the list based on their experiences collecting, hosting, and curating data. Checklist items are those that workshop participants identified as necessary to make data AI-FAIR for scientific research. Each checklist item falls under one of four general metadata categories, which together form the AI-FAIR metadata criteria. We mapped these items to relevant standards including Ecological Metadata Language ( Jones et al., 2019 ), DataCite ( DataCite Metadata Working Group, 2026 ), Schema.org ( Schema.org Community Group, 2026 ), and Croissant ( Akhtar et al., 2024 ), where the terms exist. This mapping allows the checklist to bridge domain metadata and general AI data documentation. The full, community-approved, schema and mapping will be published with the checklist; it is currently under an open review by the broader biological community to ensure clarity and support. An analogous process could be completed to develop domain-specific keys in other disciplines.
paragraphs.zh: AI-FAIR 框架提出了基础设施优先事项，可使用 AI-FAIR 清单进行评估。 该清单最初源自 ESIP AI 就绪清单（ESIP Data Readiness Cluster, 2023）和图像组学数据集卡片清单（Campolongo et al., 2026）。 在这些基础上，我们邀请研讨会参与者根据其收集、托管和整理数据的经验对该清单进行评估。 清单条目是研讨会参与者认为使数据对科学研究实现 AI-FAIR 所必需的内容。 每个清单条目都属于四个通用元数据类别之一，这些类别共同构成 AI-FAIR 元数据标准。 在相关术语存在的情况下，我们将这些条目映射到相关标准，包括生态元数据语言（Jones et al., 2019）、DataCite（DataCite Metadata Working Group, 2026）、Schema.org（Schema.org Community Group, 2026）和 Croissant（Akhtar et al., 2024）。 这一映射使该清单能够连接领域元数据与通用 AI 数据文档。 完整的、经社区认可的架构及映射将随清单一同发布；目前正接受更广泛的生物学界的公开审查，以确保其清晰性并获得支持。 可以通过类似流程在其他学科中开发领域特定的键。

paragraphs.en: Below, we define the four AI-FAIR metadata criteria, provide examples of checklist categories or items included in them, and what each criterion (or combination of criteria) enables.
paragraphs.zh: 下文将定义 AI-FAIR 的四项元数据标准，列举其中包含的清单类别或条目的示例，并说明每项标准（或多项标准的组合）所能实现的功能。

paragraphs.en: Structural metadata describe formats, schemas, organization, variables, file relationships, and other values required for machine-readable access, conforming to FAIR standards. These properties determine whether a dataset can be acquired and inserted into a machine-learning pipeline and how data exchange can more readily occur. They support an assessment of machine learning (ML) readiness , but do not by themselves establish scientific validity.
paragraphs.zh: 结构元数据描述符合FAIR标准的机器可读访问所需的格式、模式、组织方式、变量、文件关系及其他取值。 这些属性决定一个数据集能否被获取并插入机器学习流程，以及数据交换能够以何种更便捷的方式发生。 它们支持对机器学习（ML）就绪度的评估，但本身并不能确立科学有效性。

paragraphs.en: Scientific metadata describe how observations or datasets were generated and what they mean. For example, a biodiversity use may include sampling design, effort, detectability, sensor placement and calibration, itemized and categorical species data, spatial and temporal resolution, taxonomic treatment and labels, uncertainty, and experimental context. These metadata are often necessary for determining whether data are fit for the intended scientific task. Structural and scientific criteria together support an assessment of AI-readiness for particular tasks .
paragraphs.zh: 科学元数据描述观测或数据集是如何生成的，以及它们的含义是什么。 例如，生物多样性用途可能包括采样设计、工作量、可探测性、传感器布置与校准、逐项和分类的物种数据、空间和时间分辨率、分类学处理与标签、不确定性，以及实验背景。 这些元数据对于判断数据是否适用于预期科学任务往往是必要的。 结构性标准与科学性标准共同支持对特定任务的人工智能就绪性（AI-readiness）的评估。

paragraphs.en: Provenance metadata preserve the source chain, identifiers, citations, attribution requirements, checksums, and the environments and software used for processing. Provenance metadata ensures reproducibility of transformations, and paired with scientific requirements, they enable extension beyond an initial intended use and return value to the source data provider. In combination with structural requirements, these criteria support traceability .
paragraphs.zh: 溯源元数据保存源链、标识符、引用、署名要求、校验和，以及用于处理的环境和软件。 溯源元数据确保转换的可复现性，并与科学要求相结合，使其能够扩展到最初预期用途之外，并向源数据提供者回馈价值。 与结构要求相结合，这些标准支持可追溯性。

paragraphs.en: The checklist further subdivides these criteria into broad domain-agnostic categories of general information, data structure, source data, data processing, data quality, guidance and recommendations, data access, provenance and appropriate usage, and data governance. Within these categories, terms become more domain-specific. Here we provide biodiversity data examples for several elements that workshop participants found particularly important for AI-enabled science. Sampling semantics (such as experimental design, sampling effort, detection processes, instrumentation, calibration, and spatial and temporal scale) help an agent to determine whether a model can generalize beyond observed data. Processing and annotation provenance document steps, such as transformations and methods used for time-series gap filling, outlier handling, anonymization, and labeling, to help prevent data leakage and support reproducible benchmarking. Elements of the checklist pertaining to fitness and limitations ensure information provided by data sources on applicability (e.g., intended tasks, out-of-scope uses) and constraints (e.g., biases in space or time, class imbalances, distinctions between true absences and missing data) are machine-discoverable. Ontological coherence maintains label definitions with clarity and consistency. For instance, in biodiversity use cases the taxonomic backbone, resolution date, synonym handling, and identification uncertainty affect whether records from distributed sources can be combined safely and determine the appropriate process to do so. Finally, components of the checklist are meant to work synergistically. For example, elements pertaining to rights and governance ensure that machine-readable licenses, access tiers, sensitive-species flags, privacy constraints, and CARE-related permissions travel with the data and derivatives to confirm that data are fit for intended tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 该清单进一步将这些标准细分为若干宽泛的、与领域无关的类别：一般信息、数据结构、源数据、数据处理、数据质量、指南与建议、数据访问、来源与适当使用，以及数据治理。 在这些类别之内，术语变得更加领域特定。 我们在此为研讨班参与者认为对人工智能赋能的科学特别重要的若干要素提供生物多样性数据示例。 抽样语义（例如实验设计、抽样强度、探测过程、仪器设备、校准，以及空间和时间尺度）有助于智能体判断一个模型能否泛化到观测数据之外。 处理与标注来源记录了各个步骤，例如用于时间序列缺口填补、异常值处理、匿名化和标注的变换与方法，以帮助防止数据泄露并支持可复现的基准测试。 清单中与适用性和局限性相关的要素确保数据源所提供的关于适用性（例如预期任务、超范围用途）和约束（例如空间或时间上的偏差、类别不平衡、真实缺失与数据缺失之间的区别）的信息是机器可发现的。 本体一致性保证标签定义的清晰与一致。 例如，在生物多样性用例中，分类学骨架、分辨率日期、同物异名的处理以及鉴定不确定性会影响来自分布式来源的记录能否被安全地合并，并决定进行合并的适当流程。 最后，清单的各个组成部分旨在协同工作。 例如，与权利和治理相关的要素确保机器可读的许可证、访问层级、敏感物种标记、隐私约束以及与CARE原则相关的许可随数据及其衍生数据一同流转，以确认数据适用于预期任务。

paragraphs.en: We pair the checklist with an automated evaluation workflow ( Sokol & Campolongo, 2026 ). The evaluator uses an agent to retrieve available metadata, rate checklist items against a rubric, record evidence and recommendations, and provide FAIR and AI-FAIR scores (Figure 3 ). The evaluator rates each checklist item as meets , partial , does not meet , or not applicable . Each rating is assigned a set numerical value for scoring, and not applicable is excluded. The agent uses a Python script to average the item scores within each of the four AI-FAIR criteria of metadata, then maps these to their derived categories to compute scores for four components: ML-ready , AI-ready for task , Traceable , and Ethical CARE compliance . These scores then feed into the overall AI-FAIR value for a dataset alongside traditional FAIR dimensions. It is designed such that checklists for other disciplines could be substituted for the ecologically-based one with which we have started.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将这份清单与自动化评估工作流程相结合（Sokol & Campolongo, 2026）。 评估器使用智能体检索可用的元数据，根据评分规则对清单条目进行评级，记录证据和建议，并给出 FAIR 和 AI-FAIR 分数（图 3）。 评估器将每个清单条目评为“符合”、“部分符合”、“不符合”或“不适用”。 每个评级都被赋予一个固定的数值用于计分，其中“不适用”不计入。 该智能体使用 Python 脚本对元数据的四个 AI-FAIR 准则内的条目分数求平均值，然后将其映射到相应的派生类别，以计算四个组成部分的分数：ML-ready、面向任务的 AI-ready、可追溯（Traceable）以及符合伦理的 CARE。 这些分数随后与传统 FAIR 维度一起汇入数据集的总体 AI-FAIR 数值。 其设计使得其他学科的清单可以替换我们最初使用的基于生态学的清单。

paragraphs.en: The separation between evidence gathering and deterministic scoring is important to avoid circularity. An agent may locate metadata and propose ratings, but the aggregation logic is explicit and reproducible rather than estimated by a model. Evaluation output identifies strengths, missing metadata, inaccessible records, and provides concrete recommendations. Critically, these evaluation outputs also retain the evidence supporting each judgment, making the assessment reviewable by data stewards and domain experts.
paragraphs.zh: 证据收集与确定性评分之间的分离非常重要，可以避免循环论证。 智能体可以定位元数据并提出评级建议，但聚合逻辑是显式且可复现的，而不是由模型估算的。 评估输出识别优势、缺失的元数据和不可访问的记录，并提供具体的建议。 关键的是，这些评估输出还保留了支持每项判断的证据，使数据管理员和领域专家能够审阅该评估。

paragraphs.en: AI-enabled scientific discovery relies on AI agents being able to do more than simply locate and consume distributed data. Agentic workflows must be able to evaluate dataset suitability for investigating researcher-specified questions, verify usage permissions and responsibilities, and facilitate round-tripping of validated improvements to the data providers. The AI-FAIR paradigm provides a framework for these capabilities through the Question-Data-Model triangle, four complementary metadata criteria (Structural, Scientific, Provenance, Governance), a domain-interchangeable checklist, and a reusable evaluation tool. These components are generalizable beyond biodiversity data through substitution of discipline-specific values or modules into the checklist. The key is to map discipline-specific categories to their associated AI-FAIR criteria.
paragraphs.zh: AI赋能的科学发现依赖于AI智能体能够做到的远不止简单地定位和消费分布式数据。 智能体工作流必须能够评估数据集对研究者指定问题的适用性，核实使用权限与责任，并促进经过验证的改进成果回流至数据提供方。 AI-FAIR范式通过“问题-数据-模型”三角、四项互补的元数据准则（结构性、科学性、溯源、治理）、一份可跨领域互换的核查清单以及一个可复用的评估工具，为上述能力提供了框架。 通过将学科特定的取值或模块替换进核查清单，这些组件可以推广到生物多样性数据之外的领域。 关键在于将学科特定的类别映射到其对应的AI-FAIR准则。

paragraphs.en: Data publishers participating in the FAIR4AI-Bio project, including the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) and NatureServe, have begun piloting the evaluation tool to establish baseline AI-FAIR scores for their data. These quantifiable metrics measure progress toward the goal of providing AI-FAIR data, as defined by the multidisciplinary users of these data. Here we have the opportunity to engage the communities that use and produce the data in assessing and setting standards that better enable their workflows and scientific or management pursuits. Especially as AI is becoming increasingly integrated in those efforts, the AI-FAIR framework preserves disciplinary context while enabling cross-domain infrastructure. It aims to support agentic workflows without disconnecting computation from human expertise and responsibility. Most importantly, it provides a roadmap to replace one-way extraction with a roundtrip of data, evidence, attribution, and value, so that the scientists generating the data fully participate in the benefits of these AI-enabled advances. Such a fabric would not be a passive network of repositories but a distributed, governed, and continuously improving scientific knowledge system, collectively shaped by the community.
paragraphs.zh: 参与 FAIR4AI-Bio 项目的数据发布者，包括国家生态观测站网络（NEON）和 NatureServe，已开始试点使用该评估工具，为其数据建立基线 AI-FAIR 分数。 这些可量化的指标衡量了在实现提供 AI-FAIR 数据这一目标方面的进展，该目标由这些数据的多学科用户所定义。 在这里，我们有机会让使用和产生这些数据的社群参与评估和制定标准，从而更好地支持他们的工作流程以及科学或管理活动。 尤其是在 AI 日益融入这些工作的情况下，AI-FAIR 框架在实现跨领域基础设施的同时保留了学科背景。 它旨在支持智能体化的工作流程，同时不使计算与人类的专业知识和责任相脱节。 最重要的是，它提供了一条路线图，用数据、证据、归属和价值的双向循环取代单向提取，从而使产生数据的科学家能够充分参与这些 AI 驱动进步所带来的收益。 这样的结构将不是一个被动的存储库网络，而是一个由社群共同塑造的分布式、受治理且持续改进的科学知识系统。
